security.note: 1 own group base-named 'group_uom' (Manage Multiple Units of Measure) - a UI capability flag, NOT a data ACL. The 2 ir.model.access rows give base.group_user read-only on uom.uom and base.group_system full CRUD; ordinary users cannot create/edit units. Master data is therefore admin-curated and read-shared system-wide. Deletion of seeded/protected units is further blocked in Python (_unlink_except_master_data).

views.note: A single uom.uom form/list/search (Settings > Technical > Units of Measure). There is no uom.category screen because, in 19.0, categories no longer exist as a model - grouping is implicit via the relative_uom_id reference tree.

behavioral_notes.element: uom.uom v19 data model: relative_factor + relative_uom_id (_parent_store) -> computed absolute factor
behavioral_notes.observation: This is the 19.0 REFACTOR and differs from older Odoo: there is NO uom.category model, NO factor_inv, NO uom_type (reference/bigger/smaller). Instead each uom.uom optionally points at a Reference Unit via relative_uom_id (_parent_name='relative_uom_id', _parent_store=True, so parent_path is maintained), and relative_factor ('Contains', digits=0 NUMERIC) says how many of the reference this unit holds. The stored Float factor ('Absolute Quantity') is COMPUTED recursively by _compute_factor: factor = relative_factor * relative_uom_id.factor, or just relative_factor at the root. So a unit's factor is its size expressed in its category's implicit base unit (the root of its reference chain). A category is whatever set of units share a common root - made explicit only by _has_common_reference comparing parent_path prefixes. Constraint _check_factor (api.constrains) forces a root unit's relative_factor to be exactly 1.0 ('Reference unit of measure is missing.'), and the _factor_gt_zero SQL CHECK forbids relative_factor==0.

behavioral_notes.element: uom.uom._compute_quantity (the unit-conversion math; the metadata gap)
behavioral_notes.observation: _compute_quantity(qty, to_unit, round=True, rounding_method='UP', raise_if_failure=True) is the core conversion. It returns qty unchanged when self is empty/qty is 0 or self==to_unit; otherwise amount = qty * self.factor / to_unit.factor - i.e. it converts BOTH operands into the shared absolute base (factor) and rescales. When round and to_unit, it float_rounds to to_unit.rounding with the given rounding_method (default 'UP', so package/shipping math rounds up). NOTE: in this 19.0 body the method does NOT itself call _has_common_reference or raise on a category mismatch despite the raise_if_failure docstring - cross-category guarding is left to callers (e.g. product/stock) and to _has_common_reference; the bare math just divides factors. _compute_price(price, to_unit) is the INVERSE ratio: amount = price * to_unit.factor / self.factor (a smaller selling unit costs proportionally less), with no rounding. This conversion math is the classic metadata-invisible behavior.

behavioral_notes.element: uom.uom.rounding now computed from decimal.precision 'Product Unit' (not a stored per-unit field)
behavioral_notes.observation: rounding is a NON-stored compute (_compute_rounding): every unit returns 10 ** -precision where precision = decimal.precision.precision_get('Product Unit') (seeded to 2 digits by data/uom_data.xml decimal_product_uom). So ALL units share ONE system-wide rounding precision rather than per-unit rounding as in older versions; the field is kept only 'for compatibility with previous calls to uom.rounding'. The helper methods round(value, rounding_method='HALF-UP'), compare(v1, v2) and is_zero(value) all delegate to tools.float_round / float_compare / float_is_zero using that same 'Product Unit' precision - they are the supported public API for quantity arithmetic.

Seeded units are protected. _filter_protected_uoms looks up ir.model.data for module='uom' on these records, EXCLUDING the _unprotected_uom_xml_ids allowlist (product_uom_hour, product_uom_dozen, product_uom_pack_6), and returns the locked subset. _unlink_except_master_data (api.ondelete, at_uninstall=False) raises UserError listing locked units ('...used by the system and cannot be deleted... You can archive them instead.') so core units can only be archived (active=False), never deleted. _onchange_critical_fields warns when editing relative_factor on a protected unit older than a day ('existing data WON'T be updated by this change... changing core units of measure in a running database is not recommended') because changing a factor does NOT retro-convert stored quantities. _has_common_reference(other) walks both parent_path strings and returns True iff they share a non-empty prefix - the real 'same category?' test.

2 JS files, 1 OWL component (Many2OneUomField), 2 registry adds (fields:many2one_uom, fields:many2many_uom_tags), 0 patches, 2 services-ish field helpers (product_field, quantity_field); bundle ['web.assets_backend' (1)]. Many2OneUomField is a specialised many2one widget so quantity fields render their unit inline (and the many2many_uom_tags widget renders UoM tag pickers); it surfaces the unit next to a quantity rather than defining any new screen. Pure UI sugar over the uom.uom master data.

it_architecture.application: uom (Units of Measure - the reference-unit + conversion-factor master data that quantity-bearing models convert through)
logical_data_erm: uom.uom -> uom.uom (relative_uom_id: each unit points at its Reference Unit; self-referential _parent_store tree)
uom.uom -> uom.uom (related_uom_ids: inverse one2many, the units measured against this one)
uom.uom -> decimal.precision 'Product Unit' (shared rounding precision, computed not stored)
information_flows: internal: relative_factor + relative_uom_id -> _compute_factor -> stored absolute factor (recursive over the reference chain)

service: _compute_quantity / _compute_price expose unit<->unit conversion consumed by product, stock, sale, purchase, mrp, account downstream (uom is auto_install=False but a hard dependency of product)
guard: ir.model.data(module='uom') + _filter_protected_uoms gate unlink/critical-field edits on seeded units

capabilities: Maintain unit-of-measure master data (reference units + conversion factors)
Provide a shared, configurable quantity-rounding precision ('Product Unit')
Protect core/seeded units from deletion or unsafe edits
Test unit compatibility via a common reference (_has_common_reference)
value_streams: Define-Unit: create a reference unit (relative_factor=1.0) then derived units (relative_factor vs reference) -> _compute_factor materialises the absolute factor
Convert-Quantity: qty in unit A -> _compute_quantity(qty, B) = qty * A.factor / B.factor (round UP to precision) -> qty in unit B consumed by stock/sale/purchase
information_concepts: uom.uom (unit of measure, with relative_factor + computed absolute factor)
the implicit category = a set of units sharing a reference-chain root (parent_path)
organization: group_uom 'Manage Multiple Units of Measure' (UI capability toggle, not a data ACL)
policies: Reference-unit invariant: a unit with no relative_uom_id must have relative_factor==1.0 (_check_factor)
Master-data protection: seeded units (except hour/dozen/pack_6) cannot be unlinked, only archived (_unlink_except_master_data)
Safe-edit warning: changing relative_factor on an old protected unit warns that stored data is NOT retro-converted
Single shared rounding: all units round to decimal.precision 'Product Unit', not per-unit
stakeholders: System administrator / product manager (defines and curates units)
Every quantity-bearing module (product, stock, sale, purchase, mrp, account) — the conversion consumer
End user (reads units inline on quantity fields)
metrics: count of active vs archived uom.uom records
decimal.precision 'Product Unit' digits (the rounding precision in force)
reference-chain depth / number of derived units per root (data-quality signal)

classification.apqc_category: 2.0 Develop and Manage Products and Services
classification.rationale: uom is master-data FOUNDATION (Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'; Porter firm infrastructure). It owns a single tiny model (uom.uom, 9 fields, 0 routes) whose job is to define units and the math to convert quantities/prices between them - a reference data service that product depends on directly and that the whole value chain (stock, sale, purchase, mrp, account) and shop/network (services, pos) reuse for every quantity. It runs no operational document flow of its own and transforms no demand; it is shared reference data feeding every primary activity. APQC 2.0 'Develop and Manage Products and Services' is the standard home because UoM is part of the product/master-data definition layer that product itself sits in (the product record carries uom_id), and uom is a build-time dependency of product. The numbering 2.0 = 'Develop and Manage Products and Services' matches the name. A 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' (generic master/reference-data management) reading is defensible, but 2.0 is preferred because UoM is specifically product/quantity reference data tightly coupled to the product catalogue rather than enterprise-wide reference data.

standard_capabilities: Define units of measure as a reference-unit tree (relative_uom_id) with per-unit conversion factors (relative_factor)
Computed absolute factor per unit (recursive over the reference chain)
Quantity conversion (_compute_quantity, default round UP) and price conversion (_compute_price)
System-wide quantity rounding via decimal.precision 'Product Unit' + round/compare/is_zero helpers
Seeded units for count/time/length/surface/volume/weight; protection of core units (archive-not-delete)
group_uom toggle to expose multi-UoM in the UI; inline UoM widgets on quantity fields
typical_fits: Selling/stocking a product in one unit while purchasing in another (e.g. buy in Dozens, stock in Units)
Defining packaging multiples (Pack of 6) and working-time units (Days = 8 Hours)
Tuning the global quantity decimal precision via decimal.precision 'Product Unit'
Hiding multi-UoM entirely by leaving group_uom off (single-unit deployments)
common_gaps: No per-unit rounding any more - all units share one 'Product Unit' precision (behaviour change vs pre-19 factor_inv/rounding model)
_compute_quantity does not itself raise on cross-category conversion in 19.0; callers must guard compatibility
Changing a unit's factor on a live DB does not retro-convert already-stored quantities (only a warning)
No UI for bulk-defining custom unit hierarchies beyond the technical form
Categories are implicit (shared reference root) - there is no explicit uom.category record to group/report on

open_questions: Which downstream callers (product/stock/sale) still rely on the raise-on-mismatch semantics that _compute_quantity's raise_if_failure docstring implies but the 19.0 body no longer enforces - the guarding moved out of uom.
Migration impact of the 19.0 refactor (drop of uom.category/factor_inv/rounding-per-unit) on databases upgraded from <=18 - not visible in this module.
Runtime distribution of custom vs seeded units and how deeply reference chains nest in practice (models empty at capture).
